Arrange the content by having vertically stacked tabs that expand when clicked. This is an effective way to display additional information.

Add the Accordion Web Block on your Screen and as many AccordionItems as you need inside the Accordion.

Inputs.Name: MultipleItems
Inputs.Description: Set to True to allow multiple Accordion items to be expanded simultaneously. By default, False.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:

- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Blocks.Name: ProgressBar
Blocks.Description:
You can use the ProgressBar to display the current progress in a bar.
When the update frequency is high (e.g., 2 or more updates per second), the default animation speed may appear sluggish. To address this, adjust the animation speed by modifying the following CSS variables: --progress-initial-speed and --progress-speed.

To override the default animation settings, use the following CSS:

.override-speed .osui-progress-bar {
    --progress-speed: 0.1s;         /* default: 0.35s */
    --progress-initial-speed: 0.2s; /* default: 0.5s  */
}

This customization ensures that the ProgressBar remains smooth and responsive, even at high update rates.

Inputs.Name: Progress
Inputs.Description: Progress percentage. Usually a number (integer) between 0 and 100. You can also use functions and local variables.

Inputs.Name: ProgressColor
Inputs.Description:
The color that fills the bar, as progress goes up. By default, the progress color is the primary color you chose when creating the app.

To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“)
To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Inputs.Name: TrailColor
Inputs.Description:
The color of the empty part of the bar. By default,  the trail color is Neutral 4 (#DEE2E6). 

To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“)
To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Inputs.Name: Thickness
Inputs.Description: Sets the height of the ProgressBar, in pixels. By default, the thickness is "12".

Inputs.Name: OptionalConfigs
Inputs.Description: Sets additional parameters to customize the ProgressBar behavior and functionality.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples:
- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Events.Name: Initialized
Events.Description: Event triggered after the ProgressBar instance is ready.

Blocks.Name: ProgressCircle
Blocks.Description:
Circular progress indicator with a placeholder on the center of the circle. You can use this placeholder to show the current progress value.
When the update frequency is high (e.g., 2 or more updates per second), the default animation speed may appear sluggish. To address this, adjust the animation speed by modifying the following CSS variables: --progress-initial-speed and --progress-speed.

To override the default animation settings, use the following CSS:

.override-speed .osui-progress-circle {
    --progress-speed: 0.1s;         /* default: 0.35s */
    --progress-initial-speed: 0.2s; /* default: 0.5s  */
}

This customization ensures that the ProgressCircle remains smooth and responsive, even at high update rates.

Inputs.Name: Progress
Inputs.Description: Progress percentage. Usually a number from from 0 to 100.

Inputs.Name: ProgressColor
Inputs.Description:
The color that fills the circle, as progress goes up. By default, the progress color is the primary color you chose when creating the app. 

To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“)
To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Inputs.Name: Size
Inputs.Description:
Set the ProgressCircle diameter (height and width). Accepts any kind of unit (px, %, vw). By default, "100%".

Example: "30%"

Inputs.Name: TrailColor
Inputs.Description:
The color of the empty part of the circle. By default, the trail color is Neutral 4 (#DEE2E6). 

To use an RGB color, use: TextToIdentifier(“rgb(0,0,0)“)
To use an HEX color, use: TextToIdentifier(“#000000”)

Inputs.Name: Thickness
Inputs.Description: Sets the thickness of the circle that marks the progress, in pixels. By default, the thickness is "8".

Inputs.Name: OptionalConfigs
Inputs.Description: Sets additional parameters to customize the ProgressCircle behavior and functionality.

Step item to add in the Wizard pattern.

Drag the icon you want in the Icon placeholder and define the correspondent label in the Label placeholder. 
Use the Status parameter to define it's status (Past, Active, Next) and the LabelPosition to set it above (true) or alongside (false).

Inputs.Name: Status
Inputs.Description: The UI of this step, it can be Active, Next or Past

Inputs.Name: UseTopLabel
Inputs.Description: If true, label is placed above the icon.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:

- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Events.Name: OnClick
Events.Description: Event triggered after clicking on the WizardItem.

Placeholders.Description: Drag your content to this placeholder.

Placeholders.Name: Icon
Placeholders.Description: Set a number or leave it empty to show a circle icon.

Blocks.Name: SectionIndex
Blocks.Description:
Use the Section Index to organize a screen's content, enabling quick navigation within a page.

Just drag the pattern, and it will create a link to every section you have on the page. If you use a list of sections, add disable-virtualization=true through the Attributes section on the list widget containing the section patterns.

Use the parameter isFixed to define if it will stick on scroll and the TopPosition to change the distance to top. 

Set IsSmooth to true to enable animated scroll.

Inputs.Name: SmoothScrolling
Inputs.Description: If True, navigation to the destination is animated. If False, the navigation is instant. The default value is True.

Inputs.Name: IsFixed
ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:

- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Blocks.Name: OverflowMenu
Blocks.Description: Clickable element that displays hidden actions, settings, or secondary options. Use this pattern to show additional options when there is a space constraint (e.g. in toolbars or other places where a group of actions is required).

Inputs.Name: BalloonShape
Inputs.Description:
Set the balloon shape. The predefined options are:
- SoftRounded
- Rounded
- Sharp

Examples:
Entities.Shape.Rounded - the inherit style will be rounded.

By default, 4px (Entities.Shape.SoftRounded).

Default: Shape.SoftRounded

Inputs.Name: BalloonPosition
Inputs.Description:
Set the balloon’s position. The predefined options are:
- Auto 
- Top
- Top start
- Top end
- Right
- Right start
- Right end
- Bottom
- Bottom start
- Bottom end
- Left
- Left start
- Left end

Examples:
- Blank (Entities.BalloonPosition.Auto) - The placement of the balloon is automatically calculated based on the space available. This is the default.
- Entities.BalloonPosition.Right - The balloon is displayed to the right of the element.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS. Examples:

Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).

"myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.

"myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Blocks.Name: DropdownServerSide
Blocks.Description:
Dropdown block that allows you to manage large datasets in a more flexible and efficient way. The block has less out-of-the-box logic and is targeted for more advanced use cases.

Examples:
- Pagination / infinite scroll
- Search based on queries
- Custom dropdown balloon (with footer, buttons, title, etc.)

Blocks.Name: RangeSliderInterval
Blocks.Description:
Select an interval within a range of values, using two sliding handles.

For advanced options, read the official documentation:
https://refreshless.com/nouislider/

Note: To ensure the correct behavior of the component, we recommend not using different versions of it in the same page.

Inputs.Name: MinValue
Inputs.Description: Slider's minimum value.

Inputs.Name: MaxValue
Inputs.Description: Slider's maximum value.

Inputs.Name: StartingValueFrom
Inputs.Description: Default value for the interval's start. Must be between min and max values.

Inputs.Name: StartingValueTo
Inputs.Description: Default value for the interval's end. Must be between min and max values.

Inputs.Name: Orientation
Inputs.Description: Set the direction of the RangeSlider. By default, horizontal.

Inputs.Name: Size
Inputs.Description: Set the size of the Range Slider Interval. If the slider's orientation is horizontal, the size you set will be the width of the Range Slider Interval. Otherwise (vertical), the size you set will be the height. Accepts any kind of unit (px, %, vw). Default value is 100%.

Inputs.Name: OptionalConfigs
Inputs.Description: Set additional parameters to customize the RangeSliderInterval behavior and functionality.

Inputs.Name: ExtendedClass
Inputs.Description:
Add custom style classes to the Pattern. You define your custom style classes in your application using CSS.Examples:

- Blank - No custom styles are added (default value).
- "myclass" - Adds the myclass style to the UI styles being applied.
- "myclass1 myclass2" - Adds the myclass1 and myclass2 styles to the UI styles being applied.

You can also use the classes available on the OutSystems UI. For more information, see the OutSystems UI Cheat Sheet: https://outsystemsui.outsystems.com/OutsystemsUiWebsite/CheatSheet

Events.Name: Initialized
Events.Description:

OutSystems.OSUI.Patterns.RangeSliderAPI

Events.Description: Event triggered after selecting a new value on the slider. By default, the event is triggered while the user is dragging the RangeSliderInterval handler. You can use the SetRangeSliderIntervalChangeOnDragEnd to trigger the event only after the user releases it.

Params.Name: IntervalStart
Params.Description: Interval start value defined by the user.

Params.Name: IntervalEnd
Params.Description: Interval end value defined by the user.

Blocks.Description: Displays multiple items in a horizontal slide. Ideal for creating horizontal slides in smaller screens. For dynamic content, place a List directly inside the placeholder. Elements inside the placeholder represent different items.

Inputs.Description:
Set the type of navigation of the carousel. Available options:

- Arrows: show arrows on the sides
- Dots: show dots under the carousel slides
- Both: show arrows and dots on the carousel
- None: no navigation controls are shown

Inputs.Name: Height
Inputs.Description: Set a custom height for the carousel. The parameter accepts any CSS format, except percentage (library constraint). By default, 'auto'.

Inputs.Name: ItemsPerSlide
Inputs.Description:

- Desktop: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in desktop. By default, 1 item in all devices.
- Tablet: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in tablet. By default, 1 item in all devices.
- Phone: Set the number of items that are shown simultaneously in phone. By default, 1 item in all devices.

Drag to the screen, add the notification content, and bind the variable to control the visibility of the message.

Set the initial state of the Notification. If "True", the notification starts open. Use one of the following actions to change the value afterward:

- NotificationClose

Inputs.Description:
Set the Notification width. Accepts any kind of unit (px, %, vw). Default is "370px".
In case, the value defined is bigger than the screen size, the notification width will be 100%.

-Bottom
-BottomLeft
-BottomRight
-Center
-Left
-Right
-Top
-TopLeft

Date and time picker with a flat UI to be displayed inline on the screen. It can receive lists of dates with events and selection within a range of days.

For better usability and compatibility with library behaviors, you should use with an input and variable of type "text".

Previously called Calendar.

For advanced options, read the official documentation:
https://github.com/dbushell/Pikaday

Inputs.Description: Input Element Name that will trigger the element to be visible.

Inputs.Description:
Element Name (example: button) that will trigger the element to be visible.

It overrides what triggers the opening of the date picker.

Inputs.Description: Days before this date will be disabled.

Inputs.Name: MaxDate
Inputs.Description: Days after this date will be disabled.

Inputs.Name: InitialDate
Inputs.Description:
The initial selected day for the Date Picker.
If not set, it will be the current day by default.

Inputs.Name: ShowWeekNumbers
Inputs.Description: Displays the week number on the left side of the Date Picker.

Inputs.Name: FirstWeekDay
Inputs.Description:
Defines which week day should be displayed first.

0: Sunday
1: Monday
2: Tuesday
3: Wednesday
4: Thursday
5: Friday
6: Saturday

Inputs.Description: Displays a time picker below the Date Picker.

Inputs.Description: Changes the time picker to a 24 hour format.

If the string is empty, all weekdays are active.

"0,5"

0: Sunday
1: Monday
2: Tuesday
3: Wednesday
4: Thursday
5: Friday
6: Saturday

Inputs.Description:

Inputs.Description:

For better compatibility we advise using an input and variable of type "text". If that's the case, here's some of the examples that you can use:

        "MM/DD/YYYY" -> 03/23/2018
        "DD MMM YYYY" -> 23 Mar 2018

        "YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss"
        "YYYY.MM.DD HH:mm:ss"

Blocks.Name: TimePicker
Blocks.Description: Allows the user to select a time using a picker.

Inputs.Name: TimeFormat
Inputs.Description:
Set the input time format. If empty, the time format will be defined based on the Is24Hours parameter. 
Here is a list of formatting tokens that you can use:

H → Hours (24 hours)
h → Hours (12 hours)
G → Hours (12 hours), 2 digits with leading zeros
i → Minutes
s → Seconds
S → Seconds, 2 digits with leading zeros
K → AM/PM

You may escape formatting tokens using \\.

Examples:
“H:i” → 15:30
“G:i K” → 03:30 PM
”h\\hi\\m K” → 3h30m PM
”H \\ho\\ur\\s i \\m\\i\\n\\ute\\s” → 15 hours 30 minutes

Inputs.Name: Is24Hours
Inputs.Description: Set to “True” to display the time in a 24 hour format without AM/PM selection. By default, the time is displayed using a 24 hour format.

Inputs.Name: InitialTime
Inputs.Description: The initial selected time for the TimePicker. If not set, no initial time will be displayed on the input and the TimePicker will start at 12:00.

Structures.Name: SplideConfigs
Structures.Description: Structure with all configs supported by the provider.

Attributes.Name: role
Attributes.Description:
Sets a role attribute to the root element. It must be a landmark role or group.
To prevent Splide from assigning the default value (region), pass an empty string or undefined.

Attributes.Name: label
Attributes.Description: Sets an aria-label attribute to the root element. This option overwrites the attribute defined by HTML.

Attributes.Name: labelledby
Attributes.Description: Sets an aria-labelledby attribute to the root element. This option overwrites the attribute defined by HTML.

Attributes.Name: rewind
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to rewind the carousel or not. This does not work in the loop mode.

Attributes.Name: speed
Attributes.Description: The transition speed in milliseconds. If 0, the carousel immediately jumps to the target slide.

Attributes.Name: rewindSpeed
Attributes.Description: The transition speed on rewind in milliseconds. The speed value is used as default.

Attributes.Name: rewindByDrag
Attributes.Description: Allows users to rewind a carousel by drag. The rewind option must be true.

Attributes.Name: width
Attributes.Description: Defines the carousel max width, accepting the CSS format such as 10em, 80vw.

Attributes.Name: fixedWidth
Attributes.Description: Fixes width of slides, accepting the CSS format. The carousel will ignore the perPage option if this value is provided.

Attributes.Name: fixedHeight
Attributes.Description: Fixes height of slides, accepting the CSS format except for %. The carousel will ignore perPage, height and heightRatio options if this value is provided.

Attributes.Name: autoWidth
Attributes.Description: If true, the width of slides are determined by their width.

Attributes.Name: perMove
Attributes.Description: Determines the number of slides to move at once.

Attributes.Name: clones
Attributes.Description: Specifies the number of clones on each side of the loop carousel.

Attributes.Name: cloneStatus
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to add the is-active class to clones or not.

Attributes.Name: paginationDirection
Attributes.Description: Explicitly sets the pagination direction that does not only affect appearance but also shortcuts and ARIA attributes. The default value is determined by the carousel direction. Accepts 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'ttb'

Attributes.Name: easing
Attributes.Description: The timing function for the CSS transition, such as linear, ease or cubic-bezier().

Attributes.Name: noDrag
Attributes.Description: Snaps the closest slide in the drag free mode.

Attributes.Name: flickPower
Attributes.Description: Determines the power of "flick". The larger number this is, the farther the carousel runs.

Attributes.Name: flickMaxPages
Attributes.Description: Limits the number of pages to move by the flick action.

Attributes.Name: waitForTransition
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to disable any actions while the carousel is transitioning. Even if false, the carousel forcibly waits for the transition on the loop points.

Attributes.Name: arrowPath
Attributes.Description: Changes the arrow SVG path, like 'm7.61 0.807-2.12...'. The SVG size must be 40×40.

Attributes.Name: interval
Attributes.Description: The autoplay interval in milliseconds.

Attributes.Name: pauseOnHover
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to pause autoplay on mouseover or not.

Attributes.Name: pauseOnFocus
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to pause autoplay while the carousel contains the active element (focused element).

Attributes.Name: resetProgress
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to reset the autoplay progress when it is requested to start again.

Attributes.Name: lazyLoad
Attributes.Description: Enables lazy loading. Accepts true | false | 'nearby' | 'sequential'

Attributes.Name: preloadPages
Attributes.Description: Determines how many pages (not slides) around the active slide should be loaded beforehand.

Attributes.Name: wheel
Attributes.Description: Enables navigation by the mouse wheel. To use this option, set waitForTransition to be true and/or give wheelSleep duration, otherwise your carousel will immediately reach the end.

Attributes.Name: wheelMinThreshold
Attributes.Description: The threshold to cut off the small delta produced by inertia scroll.

Attributes.Name: wheelSleep
Attributes.Description: The sleep duration in milliseconds until accepting next wheel. The timer starts when the transition begins.

Attributes.Name: releaseWheel
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to release the wheel event when the carousel reaches the first or last slide so that the user can scroll the page continuously.

Attributes.Name: slideFocus
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to add tabindex="0" to visible slides or not.

Attributes.Name: focusableNodes
Attributes.Description: A selector for focusable nodes inside slides.

Attributes.Name: isNavigation
Attributes.Description: If true, the carousel makes slides clickable to navigate another carousel.

Attributes.Name: trimSpace
Attributes.Description: Determines whether to trim spaces before/after the carousel if the focus option is available.

Attributes.Name: updateOnMove
Attributes.Description: Updates the is-active status of slides just before moving the carousel.

Attributes.Name: mediaQuery
Attributes.Description: If min, the media query for breakpoints will be min-width, or otherwise, max-width.

Attributes.Name: live
Attributes.Description: Enables a live region. If isNavigation is enabled, Splide won't activate it.

Attributes.Name: destroy
Attributes.Description: Destroys the carousel

Attributes.Name: omitEnd
Attributes.Description: If true, omits some pagination dots which just changes the active slide and do not move a carousel. Also, disables a next arrow when a carousel reaches the last page.

Attributes.Name: TimeFormat
Attributes.Description:
Set the input time format. If empty, the time format will be defined based on the Is24Hours parameter. Here is a list of formatting tokens that you can use:

H → Hours (24 hours)
h → Hours (12 hours)
G → Hours (12 hours), 2 digits with leading zeros
i → Minutes
s → Seconds
S → Seconds, 2 digits with leading zeros
K → AM/PM

You may escape formatting tokens using \\.

Examples:
“H:i” → 15:30
“G:i K” → 03:30 PM
”h\\hi\\m K” → 3h30m PM
”H \\ho\\ur\\s i \\m\\i\\n\\ute\\s” → 15 hours 30 minutes

Attributes.Name: Is24Hours
Attributes.Description: Set to “True” to display the time in a 24 hour format without AM/PM selection. By default, the time is displayed using a 24 hour format.

Attributes.Name: InitialTime
Attributes.Description: The initial selected time for the TimePicker. If not set, no initial time will be displayed on the input and the TimePicker will start at 12:00.

Attributes.Name: MinTime
Attributes.Description: Set the minimum time that can be selected. Time before will be disabled.

Attributes.Name: keyboardPageMultiplier

Use this link to check all available configs: https://splidejs.com/v3/guides/events/#event-list

"move": Fired right before the slider moves..

"resized": Fired whenever Splide completes resizing the slider.

"dragged": Fired right after the user finishes dragging the slider.

Check all available events at: https://splidejs.com/v3/guides/events/#event-list

Inputs.Name: Handler
Inputs.Description: Action that will be performed once the event with the EventName occurs. Note: Please ensure that inside the JS Node, the client actions are correctly referenced. E.g. ClientActionName with no ()
